subject: Re: Atlas Sports — hosted API incentive & exit plan
messages:
From: Morgan Lee <morgan@atlas-sports.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-08T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API incentive request — Atlas migration economics

Neha,

Quick note from procurement: Atlas is running a pilot with Redwood and we are evaluating a full displacement of our current OpenAI-hosted endpoints. Before we recommend a production cutover to our execs, procurement and platforms want a formal incentive package that makes the migration economics attractive.

To be concrete: our average monthly usage for the last three months is ~1.2 billion tokens across generation + embeddings (embedding % is ~35%). Current commercial terms with our incumbent (OpenAI) include a multi-line discount and a migration credit for one-off ingestion costs. They have given us an illustrative 12-month price ladder that gets competitive at scale.

Ask: can Redwood provide a time-bound migration incentive + per-token commit tiers that would allow Atlas to justify the migration from an NPV standpoint? Also we need to see line items for token rate, embedding rate, egress, and any observational/legal credits (SOC 2 evidence, audit support).

I can share an excerpt from our usage report (attaching a high-level CSV). Happy to do a 30-min call next week to walk through numbers.

Thanks,
Morgan
Morgan Lee
Head of Platform Procurement
Atlas Sports

Attachment: Atlas_usage_report_May2026.csv (CSV, 48KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Morgan Lee <morgan@atlas-sports.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-09T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API incentive request — Atlas migration economics

Morgan — thanks for the clarity and the data. Appreciate the attachment.

High level response and options (quick summary):
- Migration incentive: we can provide a one-time migration credit to offset ingestion/engineering costs (suggested: $150K one-time) plus a 3-month ramp credit applied to token billing.
- Commit tiers (hosted API, per-token):
  * Tier A (12-month commit, 300M tokens/mo avg): $0.00075 per generation token, embeddings at $0.00035 per token.
  * Tier B (12-month commit, 600M tokens/mo avg): $0.00060 per generation token, embeddings $0.00028 per token.
  * Tier C (12-month enterprise commit, 1.2B tokens/mo avg): $0.00048 per generation token, embeddings $0.00022 per token.
- Escape / short-term protection: 60-day notice with a pro-rata true-up; we can include a limited cloud-exit credit if Atlas migrates away to an IaaS provider within first 12 months (details negotiable).
- Other items: no separate egress line for hosted API (included), but we will list egress explicitly for Private/Dedicated options. SOC 2 and evidence: we will provide SOC 2 Type II report and auditing artifacts via our secure share.

I've attached a formal offer (redwood-escape-offer-v1.pdf) that spells the numbers and a suggested mutual action plan (POC timeline, security review, legal checklist). If the above structure looks promising, next step would be a joint MLP (mutual action plan) with legal and procurement milestones.

Would love to do a call early next week to walk through the SLA/true-up language — when are you available?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-escape-offer-v1.pdf (PDF, 220KB)

From: Morgan Lee <morgan@atlas-sports.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API incentive request — Atlas migration economics

Neha — thanks, this is helpful. A few clarifying points from procurement/legal: 
1) Embedding pricing: does the embedding token definition match ours (input tokens only) or do you bill combined input/output? We need line-item parity vs incumbent.
2) True-up mechanics: can you walk me through an example true-up calculation and when it would kick in? Is there a cap on overage rate?
3) Cloud-exit credit: procurement likes the concept but wants a firm schedule (e.g., credits payable if we shift to another hosted vendor within 12 months, up to X% of committed spend).
4) SLA: need 99.9% availability guarantee for inference endpoints with remediation/credit schedule.

Legal will want to see the redlines in DocuSign. Can you provide a one-page Excel with the line items and example math (month-by-month cost comparison vs incumbent) so our finance team can plug into their model?

Also cc'ing our SRE (procurement@atlas-sports.com) — they'd like a short tech session on tokenization behavior and KV cache behavior to understand latency implications.

Morgan

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Hosted API incentive request — Atlas migration economics

Team — looping you in on Atlas (attached usage). Procurement has pushed for a firm migration incentive and a cloud-exit credit. Proposed structure below; please review and advise on feasibility for finance/legal: 

Proposed commercial structure (internal):
- 12-month hosted API commitment with monthly true-up. Baseline commitment = 12 x expected monthly tokens.
- Breakpoints (monthly averages): 300M / 600M / 1.2B — with per-token rates previously shared.
- Migration incentives: $150K one-time credit + 3 months 50% token credit applied to billing (to ease ramp).
- Cloud-exit protection: if Atlas moves to a different hosted vendor within 12 months, we will credit up to 20% of their committed spend (paid back over next 3 invoices) — legal to confirm language.
- SLA: target 99.9% for hosted inference; remediation via service credits, legal to scope exact formula.

Questions for finance/legal:
1) Is the proposed cloud-exit credit acceptable as an up-to-20%-of-commit line-item? How does this impact revenue recognition?
2) If Atlas over-indexes on embeddings (they said ~35%), do we want a blended token model or separate line items? Current offer uses separate embedding rates.
3) For reporting: what audit evidence do we need to provide to satisfy procurement? (SOC2 + usage export + request-level traces?)

Marissa — can you run a quick economics sensitivity on the two breakpoints vs incumbent pricing (I know you have the benchmarking slides)?

Thanks — looking to have a negotiated term sheet by end of next week.

Neha

Attachment: redwood-escape-offer-v1.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Morgan Lee <morgan@atlas-sports.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API incentive request — Atlas migration economics (next steps)

Morgan — thanks for the back-and-forth. Short note from my side:

We can commit to the commercial structure Neha outlined with two asks from Atlas: a) a 60-90 day POC that includes a short technical validation (tokenization/latency) and b) a signed term sheet that locks the credit structure.

I'll schedule a 45-min technical session with our SRE lead to run through KV cache behavior and the embedding pipeline. Also, Neha — legal will prepare a term sheet draft with the cloud-exit credit language; would appreciate Marissa running the cost sensitivity before we send to Atlas legal.

Morgan — are you available for a kickoff call on Tuesday 2026-06-22 10:00am PT? If so, we'll send a calendar invite and a one-page cost workbook the same day.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
